html:
The Agwamin are a small Aboriginal Australian people of inland north Queensland, west of the Atherton Tableland. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Little is written about them. Their name and territory come mainly from the surveys of Norman Tindale, who mapped Aboriginal peoples across the continent in the 20th century. Neighbours on the map include the Takalak, the Mbabaram and the Walangama. Like them, they lived by hunting and gathering in dry ranges and river country until cattle stations and the north Queensland gold rushes of the late 1800s took over the land. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
